headline: Telangana HC: specific performance refused where sale was contingent on pending excise case
reference: M/s Intercorp Engineers v. M/s Kumar Power Products Pvt Ltd & Anr., Appeal Suit No. 117 of 2012, Telangana High Court, 17 November 2026
summary_points: Issue: Could the buyer get specific performance of a 2003 sale agreement when the seller's excise dues case was pending before CEGAT and the property was attached?
Held: The 13.05.2003 endorsement made the agreement contingent on CEGAT's final orders, so the suit filed on 05.04.2005 was premature; appeal dismissed without costs.
Court noted Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act requires continuous readiness and willingness; a two-year silence after 13.05.2003 suggested abandonment.
A pre-suit legal notice is not statutorily mandatory, so its absence does not make a specific performance suit bad in law.
Seller directed to deposit ₹5 lakh with 18% interest from 24.01.2011 and ₹4,210 within 30 days; buyer may withdraw.
who_is_affected: Buyers and sellers under agreements of sale tied to pending tax or excise disputes or attachments, and lawyers handling specific performance suits.
action_required: Draft contingent conditions in sale agreements clearly and, if you are the buyer, show continuous readiness and willingness, including financial capacity, without long delays in suing.

Telangana High Court on specific performance where a sale agreement depends on a pending excise case.

In Intercorp Engineers v. Kumar Power Products (AS No. 117 of 2012, decided 17 November 2026), the buyer sought specific performance of a 2003 agreement of sale for ₹95 lakh. The seller's property was under attachment, and an excise case was pending before CEGAT.

The Division Bench held that the seller's endorsement dated 13.05.2003, postponing the agreement till final CEGAT orders, made it a contingent contract. The suit was therefore premature.

Key takeaways:
- Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act requires continuous readiness and willingness. The buyer's two-year silence suggested abandonment.
- A pre-suit legal notice is not statutorily mandatory.
- The seller must refund ₹5 lakh with 18% interest and ₹4,210 stamp duty within 30 days.

For deal lawyers and CAs, the lesson is to document contingencies precisely and to act promptly when rights are at stake.
